Opposite Party :- State Of U.P. And 3 Others
Counsel for Applicant :- Vikash Chandra Tiwari
Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Krishan Pahal,J.
1.
List has been revised.
As informed by learned AGA, notice to the informant has been served on 29.01.2025 but none is present on behalf of the informant.

2. Heard Sri Vikash Chandra Tiwari , learned counsel for the applicant and Sri Arun Kumar Mishra,
learned A.G.A. for the State and perused the record.
3.
Applicant seeks bail in Case Crime No. 152 of 2024 , under Sections 376(AB) of IPC and Sections 5m/6 of POCSO Act, Police Station Kaushambi, District Ghaziabad, during the pendency of trial.

4. As per prosecution story, the applicant is stated to have outraged the modesty of the victim aged about 14 years on 02.04.2024 at about 4 p.m. after barging into her house and he has locked the door from inside.
After much persuasion, the applicant is stated to have opened the door and ran away from the place of occurrence.

sentences.text: 5. Learned counsel for the applicant has argued that the applicant is absolutely innocent and has been falsely implicated in the present case.
He has nothing to do with the said offence as alleged in the FIR.
The FIR is delayed by more than one day and there is no explanation of the said delay caused.
6. Learned counsel has also stated that the allegations are per se false.

Initially, the FIR was instituted regarding outraging the modesty only but subsequently the allegations have been escalated to that of rape in the statement of the victim recorded under section 183 BNSS whereby she has stated that the applicant had raped her and had closed the door from inside but her mother came there and had locked the applicant inside the room but he broke open the room and ran away from the place of occurrence.
7.
It is further stated that there is no observation of the Investigating Officer regarding lock being broken by the applicant.
The said allegations are false.
The victim is aged about 16 years as per ossification test report.
8. There is no criminal history of the applicant.
The applicant is languishing in jail since 04.05.2024 and he is ready to cooperate with trial.
In case, the applicant is released on bail, he will not misuse the liberty of bail.

9. Per contra, learned AGA has vehemently opposed the bail application but unable to dispute the submissions raised by the learned counsel for the applicant and also the fact that the applicant has no criminal history.

10. Considering the facts and circumstances of the case, submissions made by learned counsel for the parties and taking into consideration the delay in FIR and taking into account the statement of the victim recorded under section 183 BNSS, I find it a fit case to release the applicant on bail.
The bail application is allowed.

11. Let the applicant- Akash , who is involved in aforementioned case crime be released on bail on his furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned subject to following conditions.
Further, before issuing the release order, the sureties be verified.
i) The applicant shall not tamper with the evidence during trial.
ii) The applicantshall not pressurise/intimidate with the prosecution witnesses.
iii) The applicantshall appear before the trial court on the date fixed.
12. In case of breach of any of the above conditions, it shall be a ground for cancellation of bail.

13. It is made clear that observations made in granting bail to the applicant shall not in any way affect the learned trial Judge in forming his independent opinion based on the testimony of the Akash vs State Of U.P.
